items.title: Josephine Davies interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 14, 2025
items.q: trying to get a gig at places like Ron Scott’s where I love playing Ronnie Scott’s and it’s very high profile and it’s a great venue, and incredibly hard to get a gig there.

ctx.x: If you talk to current jazz musicians here in the States about the state of jazz, it’s usually not an uplifting conversation. Over here we have -- academia keeps the music alive I think. That’s where it mostly lives. Or in the wealthy institutions. But club-wise it’s not a – in comparison to what – where are the good old days, I’m not sure which days they were. But I’m wondering about how hard is it to make a living as a jazz musician in England?

Yeah. It’s one of those questions that again it depends on the mood of the person speaking probably. I think it is hard. I think it has got harder. There is a sense sometimes of no one’s got any money and there are so many bands trying to get the same gigs and every year there are more bands. Most of them are fantastic. And there are fewer pubs and the pubs that there are lose their funding, and the travel around the U.K. is difficult, everything is expensive, traffic is horrendous, etcetera, etcetera. And so…

but a sense of how can I make the current world work for me. Because I think it’s always good to bear in mind that yes there are things that are more challenging, more difficult, and potentially terrible. But there are also things that have become better for a lot of people. And I think it’s important for me to remember that and feel that I am still living this incredibly creative, spontaneous, free life, which is extraordinary to have that and to be able to really do what I want on a daily basis. I mean I have…
